literature.headline_zh: 人腺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人腺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 基因组和系统发育分析证实HAdV-3-TZ01属于物种B中的HAdV-3,并且其基因组骨架与当前流行的HAdV-3株高度保守。HAdV-3-TZ01在多种人类呼吸道相关细胞系(包括A549、H3122、BEAS-2B、MRC-5和HEK293FT细胞)中表现出高效的病毒基因组扩增,而在小鼠L929细胞中,病毒基因组扩增则受到明显限制。在A549-荧光素酶异种移植模型中,HAdV-3-TZ01的瘤内给药显著抑制了肿瘤进展。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1912909]
经鼻腔接种两剂rAdTS 疫苗接种可保护小鼠免受致命性皮下和口服克氏锥虫感染,与对照小鼠相比,表现出较低的寄生虫血症和较高的存活率。经鼻腔接种的疫苗在寄生虫暴露后显示出最高的免疫应答反应,其在黏膜组织和血清中产生的TS特异性IgA与寄生虫血症呈负相关。 [10.1093/infdis/jiag227]
E1A和E3-19K均被检测到存在于IRE1a复合物中,表明病毒采用了逐步的调控机制。 [10.1091/mbc.e26-06-0273]
对122例样本进行全基因组测序,结果显示HAdV-B(62.3%)、HAdV-C(34.4%)和HAdV-F(3.3%)。 [10.1093/ve/veag064]
呼吸道病原体的总体阳性率为69.14%。肺炎支原体(Mp)(26.94%)、人类鼻病毒(HRV)(16.29%)和人腺病毒(HADV)(9.00%)是最常见的病原体。在阳性样本中检测到19.85%的混合感染,其中双感染最为常见。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14531-9]

papers.title: Whole genome sequencing reveals a decade of human adenovirus B114 circulation in England
papers.abstract: Background Human Mastadenovirus B (HAdV-B) causes ocular and respiratory infections and is capable of causing outbreaks in healthcare settings. HAdV-B114, a recombinant genotype only formally recognised in 2023, has been reported predominantly from Germany, the USA, China and Japan; genomic data from UK clinical settings remain limited. This study analysed 68 HAdV-B whole genomes from ocular and respiratory-associated samples collected at a Nottingham hospital across the pre- and post-COVID-19 restriction periods (2017-2023). Methods Clinical samples typed positive for HAdV-B by partial hexon Sanger sequencing were selected for whole-genome sequencing using a novel over-lapping PCR amplicon strategy, sequenced on the Oxford Nanopore Technologies PromethION platform. Phylogenetic and pairwise difference analyses were used to characterise genotype composition and genomic relatedness. SimPlot and amino-acid comparison characterised divergence between sub-lineages. Results Whole-genome phylogenetics confirmed that two species B genotypes were detected in Nottingham University Hospitals between 2017-23: HAdV-B114 (n=56) and HAdV-B7 (n=12). HAdV-B114 was detected before and after COVID-19 restrictions, with an increase in 2022-2023, consistent with post-restriction expansion of a pre-existing lineage. Pairwise difference analysis identified 24 genomically identical B114 sequences; associated metadata argued against a single nosocomial transmission chain interpretation, with the pattern more consistent with repeated detection of a widely circulating community strain, with the possibility of localised onward transmission. Within the B114 clade, multiple monophyletic groups were identified by whole-genome phylogenetics. Conclusions This study adds whole-genome resolution to the existing UK HAdV-B114 data, demonstrates the utility of WGS for clinical adenovirus surveillance and shows the benefits of combining epidemiological data with genomic analysis.

This study analysed 68 HAdV-B whole genomes from ocular and respiratory-associated samples collected at a Nottingham hospital across the pre- and post-COVID-19 restriction periods (2017-2023). Methods Clinical samples typed positive for HAdV-B by partial hexon Sanger sequencing were selected for whole-genome sequencing using a novel over-lapping PCR amplicon strategy, sequenced on the Oxford Nanopore Technologies PromethION platform. Phylogenetic and pairwise difference analyses were used to characterise genotype composition and genomic relatedness. SimPlot and amino-acid comparison characterised divergence between sub-lineages. Results Whole-genome phylogenetics confirmed that two species B genotypes were detected in Nottingham University Hospitals between 2017-23: HAdV-B114 (n=56) and HAdV-B7 (n=12). HAdV-B114 was detected before and after COVID-19 restrictions, with an increase in 2022-2023, consistent with post-restriction expansion of a pre-existing lineage. Pairwise difference analysis identified 24 genomically identical B114 sequences; associated metadata argued against a single nosocomial transmission chain interpretation, with the pattern more consistent with repeated detection of a widely circulating community strain, with the possibility of localised onward transmission. Within the B114 clade, multiple monophyletic groups were identified by whole-genome phylogenetics. Conclusions This study adds whole-genome resolution to the existing UK HAdV-B114 data, demonstrates the utility of WGS for clinical adenovirus surveillance and shows the benefits of combining epidemiological data with genomic analysis.
papers.title_original: Whole genome sequencing reveals a decade of human adenovirus B114 circulation in England

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the circulation of human adenovirus B114 in England over a decade, addressing the limited genomic data available from UK clinical settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analysed 68 HAdV-B whole genomes from ocular and respiratory-associated samples collected at a Nottingham hospital between 2017 and 2023, encompassing both pre- and post-COVID-19 restriction periods.
analysis.methods: Clinical samples typed positive for HAdV-B by partial hexon Sanger sequencing were selected for whole-genome sequencing using a novel overlapping PCR amplicon strategy, sequenced on the Oxford Nanopore Technologies PromethION platform.
analysis.main_results: Whole-genome phylogenetics confirmed that two species B genotypes were detected in Nottingham University Hospitals between 2017-23: HAdV-B114 (n=56) and HAdV-B7 (n=12). HAdV-B114 was detected before and after COVID-19 restrictions, with an increase in 2022-2023, consistent with post-restriction expansion of a pre-existing lineage. Pairwise difference analysis identified 24 genomically identical B114 sequences.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that HAdV-B114 is a widely circulating community strain, with the possibility of localised onward transmission, rather than a single nosocomial transmission chain.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical genomic data for understanding the epidemiology of HAdV-B114 in the UK, supporting the use of whole-genome sequencing for clinical adenovirus surveillance and informing future public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single hospital, which may affect generalisability, and the absence of detailed statistical analyses. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the circulation of human adenovirus B114 in England over a decade, focusing on genomic data from Nottingham University Hospitals between 2017 and 2023. Using whole-genome sequencing, the researchers identified 56 HAdV-B114 genomes and 12 HAdV-B7 genomes, with HAdV-B114 detected both before and after the implementation of COVID-19 restrictions. The results showed an increase in HAdV-B114 cases during 2022-2023, suggesting post-restriction expansion of a pre-existing lineage. Pairwise difference analysis revealed 24 genomically identical B114 sequences, indicating repeated detection of a community strain rather than a single nosocomial transmission. The study highlights the importance of whole-genome sequencing in clinical adenovirus surveillance and adds to the understanding of HAdV-B114 in the UK. However, the study's focus on a single hospital may limit its generalisability, and the absence of detailed statistical analyses affects the strength of the evidence.

papers.title: Biological characterization of a clinical human adenovirus type 3 isolate with oncolytic potential
papers.abstract: Introduction Human adenovirus type 3 (HAdV-3) is a major adenovirus type associated with respiratory infections in China. Despite its clinical importance, the biological characteristics and potential biomedical applications of contemporary circulating HAdV-3 strains remain incompletely understood. Naturally occurring species B adenoviruses also remain relatively underexplored as potential starting backbones for oncolytic virotherapy. This study aimed to characterize a contemporary clinical HAdV-3 isolate and evaluate its viral genome amplification, apoptosis induction, and antitumor activity. Methods A clinical HAdV-3 isolate, designated HAdV-3-TZ01, was recovered from a throat swab specimen from a patient with adenovirus-associated respiratory disease. Viral identity and genomic characteristics were determined using multiplex PCR, Sanger sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and recombination analysis. Viral genome amplification kinetics were evaluated in human respiratory-related and tumor-derived cell lines and a murine cell line by quantitative PCR. Comparative apoptosis induction by HAdV-3-TZ01 and HAdV-5 was assessed in 293F cells infected at a low multiplicity of infection using Annexin V/PI flow cytometry. Antitumor activity was evaluated following repeated intratumoral administration of HAdV-3-TZ01 in an A549-luciferase xenograft model in BALB/c-nu nude mice, with tumor growth and bioluminescence monitored longitudinally. Results Genomic and phylogenetic analyses confirmed that HAdV-3-TZ01 belonged to HAdV-3 within species B and exhibited a genomic backbone highly conserved with contemporary circulating HAdV-3 strains. A short putative HAdV-7-derived recombinant fragment was identified. HAdV-3-TZ01 showed efficient viral genome amplification in multiple human respiratory-related cell lines, including A549, H3122, BEAS-2B, MRC-5, and HEK293FT cells, whereas genome amplification was markedly restricted in murine L929 cells. HAdV-3-TZ01 induced a significantly higher proportion of late apoptotic cells than HAdV-5 in 293F cells under low-multiplicity infection conditions, although the absolute increase in total apoptosis was modest. In the A549-luciferase xenograft model, intratumoral administration of HAdV-3-TZ01 significantly suppressed tumor progression. By day 43, mean tumor volume was reduced by approximately 54% and tumor-associated bioluminescence by approximately 50% compared with mock-treated controls. No significant body-weight loss or overt signs of distress were observed under the experimental conditions. Conclusion HAdV-3-TZ01 retains the characteristic human epithelial tropism of HAdV-3 and exhibits efficient viral genome amplification in human epithelial-derived cells, apoptosis induction, and measurable antitumor activity in vivo. The apoptosis difference between HAdV-3-TZ01 and HAdV-5 should be interpreted cautiously because the analysis was limited to 293F cells and did not establish a tumor-specific pro-apoptotic mechanism. As an unmodified respiratory pathogen, HAdV-3-TZ01 should not be considered a directly translatable therapeutic agent. Rather, these findings support HAdV-3-TZ01 as a potential starting backbone for future genetic engineering aimed at improving tumor selectivity and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes a clinical isolate of human adenovirus type 3 (HAdV-3), HAdV-3-TZ01, and evaluates its potential for oncolytic virotherapy. The research aimed to assess its genome amplification, apoptosis induction, and antitumor activity. HAdV-3-TZ01 was identified as belonging to species B and showed efficient genome amplification in human respiratory-related cell lines, while its amplification was restricted in murine cells. In a xenograft model, HAdV-3-TZ01 significantly suppressed tumor progression. However, the apoptosis difference between HAdV-3-TZ01 and HAdV-5 was observed only in 293F cells, and the study cautions against assuming a tumor-specific pro-apoptotic mechanism. The findings suggest HAdV-3-TZ01 could serve as a potential backbone for genetic engineering to enhance tumor selectivity and safety. The study's evidence is moderate due to its limited scope and lack of broader validation.

papers.title_zh: 一种具有溶瘤潜力的临床人腺病毒型3分离株的生物学特征
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Human adenovirus type 3 (HAdV-3) is a major adenovirus type associated with respiratory infections in China. Despite its clinical importance, the biological characteristics and potential biomedical applications of contemporary circulating HAdV-3 strains remain incompletely understood. Naturally occurring species B adenoviruses also remain relatively underexplored as potential starting backbones for oncolytic virotherapy. This study aimed to characterize a contemporary clinical HAdV-3 isolate and evaluate its viral genome amplification, apoptosis induction, and antitumor activity. Methods A clinical HAdV-3 isolate, designated HAdV-3-TZ01, was recovered from a throat swab specimen from a patient with adenovirus-associated respiratory disease. Viral identity and genomic characteristics were determined using multiplex PCR, Sanger sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and recombination analysis. Viral genome amplification kinetics were evaluated in human respiratory-related and tumor-derived cell lines and a murine cell line by quantitative PCR. Comparative apoptosis induction by HAdV-3-TZ01 and HAdV-5 was assessed in 293F cells infected at a low multiplicity of infection using Annexin V/PI flow cytometry. Antitumor activity was evaluated following repeated intratumoral administration of HAdV-3-TZ01 in an A549-luciferase xenograft model in BALB/c-nu nude mice, with tumor growth and bioluminescence monitored longitudinally. Results Genomic and phylogenetic analyses confirmed that HAdV-3-TZ01 belonged to HAdV-3 within species B and exhibited a genomic backbone highly conserved with contemporary circulating HAdV-3 strains. A short putative HAdV-7-derived recombinant fragment was identified. HAdV-3-TZ01 showed efficient viral genome amplification in multiple human respiratory-related cell lines, including A549, H3122, BEAS-2B, MRC-5, and HEK293FT cells, whereas genome amplification was markedly restricted in murine L929 cells. HAdV-3-TZ01 induced a significantly higher proportion of late apoptotic cells than HAdV-5 in 293F cells under low-multiplicity infection conditions, although the absolute increase in total apoptosis was modest. In the A549-luciferase xenograft model, intratumoral administration of HAdV-3-TZ01 significantly suppressed tumor progression. By day 43, mean tumor volume was reduced by approximately 54% and tumor-associated bioluminescence by approximately 50% compared with mock-treated controls. No significant body-weight loss or overt signs of distress were observed under the experimental conditions. Conclusion HAdV-3-TZ01 retains the characteristic human epithelial tropism of HAdV-3 and exhibits efficient viral genome amplification in human epithelial-derived cells, apoptosis induction, and measurable antitumor activity in vivo. The apoptosis difference between HAdV-3-TZ01 and HAdV-5 should be interpreted cautiously because the analysis was limited to 293F cells and did not establish a tumor-specific pro-apoptotic mechanism. As an unmodified respiratory pathogen, HAdV-3-TZ01 should not be considered a directly translatable therapeutic agent. Rather, these findings support HAdV-3-TZ01 as a potential starting backbone for future genetic engineering aimed at improving tumor selectivity and safety.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言 人腺病毒型3(HAdV-3)是中国与呼吸道感染相关的主要腺病毒类型。尽管其在临床上具有重要性,但当前流行HAdV-3株的生物学特征及其潜在的生物医学应用仍不完全清楚。天然存在的物种B腺病毒也尚未被充分探索作为溶瘤病毒治疗的潜在骨架。本研究旨在表征一种当代临床HAdV-3分离株,并评估其病毒基因组扩增、凋亡诱导和抗肿瘤活性。方法 从一名与腺病毒相关呼吸道疾病患者咽拭子样本中分离出一种临床HAdV-3分离株,命名为HAdV-3-TZ01。通过多重PCR、Sanger测序、全基因组测序、系统发育分析和重组分析确定病毒的身份和基因组特征。通过定量PCR评估HAdV-3-TZ01在人类呼吸道相关细胞系、肿瘤来源细胞系和小鼠细胞系中的病毒基因组扩增动力学。使用Annexin V/PI流式细胞术,在低感染复数条件下比较HAdV-3-TZ01和HAdV-5在293F细胞中的凋亡诱导情况。在BALB/c-nu裸鼠的A549-荧光素酶异种移植模型中,评估HAdV-3-TZ01重复瘤内给药后的抗肿瘤活性,并纵向监测肿瘤生长和生物发光情况。结果 基因组和系统发育分析证实HAdV-3-TZ01属于物种B中的HAdV-3,并且其基因组骨架与当前流行的HAdV-3株高度保守。鉴定出一个短的可能来源于HAdV-7的重组片段。HAdV-3-TZ01在多种人类呼吸道相关细胞系(包括A549、H3122、BEAS-2B、MRC-5和HEK293FT细胞)中表现出高效的病毒基因组扩增,而在小鼠L929细胞中,病毒基因组扩增则受到明显限制。在A549-荧光素酶异种移植模型中,HAdV-3-TZ01的瘤内给药显著抑制了肿瘤进展。到第43天时,与假处理对照组相比,平均肿瘤体积减少了约54%,肿瘤相关生物发光减少了约50%。在实验条件下未观察到显著的体重减轻或明显的不适迹象。结论 HAdV-3-TZ01保留了HAdV-3的人类上皮细胞嗜性特征,并在人类上皮来源细胞中表现出高效的病毒基因组扩增、凋亡诱导以及体内可测量的抗肿瘤活性。由于分析仅限于293F细胞且未建立肿瘤特异性促凋亡机制,HAdV-3-TZ01与HAdV-5之间的凋亡差异应谨慎解读。作为一种未经修饰的呼吸道病原体,HAdV-3-TZ01不应被视为可以直接用于治疗的药物。然而,这些发现支持HAdV-3-TZ01作为未来基因工程的潜在骨架,以提高肿瘤选择性和安全性。

papers.title: Intranasal Vaccination With Recombinant Human Adenovirus Encoding trans-Sialidase Gene Protects Mice From Lethal Subcutaneous and Oral Trypanosoma cruzi Challenges.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The majority of new cases of Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, have been associated with oral infection. Thus, it is reasonable that any vaccine formulation developed should elicit systemic and mucosal immunity. METHODS: Antigen-specific T-cell, B-cell, antibody-secreting cell, IgG, IgA, cytokine, and parasite DNA were assessed in Balb/c mice immunized with a recombinant adenovirus replication-deficient vector encoding the parasitic trans-sialidase (rAdTS) and challenged with T. cruzi trypomastigotes. RESULTS: A 2-dose intranasal (IN) rAdTS administration protected mice from lethal subcutaneous and oral parasitic challenges, displaying lower parasitemia and higher survival than control mice. Although intramuscular (IM) rAdTS immunization seemed more immunogenic for CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, IN vaccinees presented the highest responses after parasite exposure. Oral parasitic challenge triggered differential cytokine and cytotoxic transcriptome profiles in the hearts of IM and IN vaccinees. IM and IN rAdTS vaccinations induced high TS-specific IgG and subclass titers in the serum, with predominance of IgG-secreting cells in the spleen and draining lymph nodes. Only IN vaccinees produced TS-specific IgA in mucosal tissues and serum, which showed inverse correlation with parasitemia in vivo. Serum samples from the IN rAdTS vaccinees significantly inhibited parasite invasion in vitro relative to IM counterparts. In addition, IN vaccinees had very low levels of parasite DNA in parasite-reservoir tissues upon oral parasitic challenge relative to IM counterparts. CONCLUSIONS: IN rAdTS vaccination can effectively protect mice against acute Chagas disease caused by lethal distinct T. cruzi challenges, providing an interesting alternative for future vaccine clinical trials.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the protective efficacy of a recombinant human adenovirus encoding the trans-sialidase gene against Trypanosoma cruzi infection, addressing the need for vaccines that can induce both systemic and mucosal immunity to combat Chagas disease, which is primarily transmitted through oral routes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved Balb/c mice immunized with a recombinant adenovirus replication-deficient vector encoding the parasitic trans-sialidase (rAdTS) and challenged with Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes. The design included both intranasal (IN) and intramuscular (IM) vaccination routes, with comparisons made between vaccinees and control mice.
analysis.methods: The researchers assessed antigen-specific T-cell, B-cell, antibody-secreting cell, IgG, IgA, cytokine, and parasite DNA responses in mice vaccinated with rAdTS. They also evaluated the in vitro inhibitory capacity of serum samples from vaccinated mice against parasite invasion.
analysis.main_results: Two doses of intranasal rAdTS vaccination protected mice from lethal subcutaneous and oral T. cruzi challenges, resulting in lower parasitemia and higher survival rates compared to control mice. IN vaccinees showed the highest immune responses after parasite exposure, with TS-specific IgA production in mucosal tissues and serum inversely correlated with parasitemia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that intranasal vaccination with rAdTS can induce robust immune responses that effectively protect against T. cruzi infection, offering a promising strategy for vaccine development against Chagas disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the potential of intranasal adenoviral vaccines for preventing Chagas disease, particularly in contexts where oral transmission is prevalent, and may inform future vaccine trials and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mouse models, which may not fully translate to human outcomes. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates clear protective effects in vivo and correlates immune responses with reduced parasitemia.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the protective efficacy of intranasal vaccination with a recombinant human adenovirus encoding the trans-sialidase gene against Trypanosoma cruzi infection in mice. The research aimed to address the need for vaccines that can elicit both systemic and mucosal immunity, as Chagas disease is primarily transmitted through oral routes. The study involved Balb/c mice immunized with the rAdTS vector and challenged with T. cruzi trypomastigotes, comparing intranasal and intramuscular vaccination routes. Results showed that intranasal vaccination significantly reduced parasitemia and increased survival rates compared to control mice, with the highest immune responses observed in this group. The findings suggest that intranasal rAdTS vaccination could be a promising strategy for preventing Chagas disease, potentially offering an alternative for future vaccine trials. The study's results are strong, but its reliance on mouse models limits direct applicability to humans.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及接种了重组腺病毒复制缺陷型媒介编码寄生虫转唾液酸酶(rAdTS)的Balb/c小鼠,并挑战其克氏锥虫裂殖体。研究设计包括经鼻腔(IN)和经肌肉(IM)疫苗接种接种途径,并比较了疫苗与对照小鼠之间的差异。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员评估了接种rAdTS的小鼠对克氏锥虫的抗原特异性T细胞、B细胞、抗体分泌细胞、IgG、IgA、细胞因子和寄生虫DNA反应。他们还评估了接种小鼠血清样本在体外对寄生虫入侵的抑制能力。
elements_zh.main_results: 经鼻腔接种两剂rAdTS 疫苗接种可保护小鼠免受致命性皮下和口服克氏锥虫感染,与对照小鼠相比,表现出较低的寄生虫血症和较高的存活率。经鼻腔接种的疫苗在寄生虫暴露后显示出最高的免疫应答反应,其在黏膜组织和血清中产生的TS特异性IgA与寄生虫血症呈负相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,经鼻腔接种的疫苗接种携带rAdTS可诱导强效的免疫应答,有效保护小鼠免受克氏锥虫感染,为开发针对克氏锥虫病的疫苗策略提供了有前景的方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为通过经鼻腔腺病毒疫苗预防克氏锥虫病提供了重要的见解,特别是在口服传播感染高发的环境中,可能为未来的疫苗试验和公共卫生策略提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于小鼠模型,可能无法完全反映人类结果。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它在体内展示了明确的保护效果,并且将免疫应答与寄生虫血症减少相关联。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the protective efficacy of a recombinant human adenovirus encoding the trans-sialidase gene against Trypanosoma cruzi infection, addressing the need for vaccines that can induce both systemic and mucosal immunity to combat Chagas disease, which is primarily transmitted through oral routes.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved Balb/c mice immunized with a recombinant adenovirus replication-deficient vector encoding the parasitic trans-sialidase (rAdTS) and challenged with Trypanosoma cruzi trypomastigotes. The design included both intranasal (IN) and intramuscular (IM) vaccination routes, with comparisons made between vaccinees and control mice.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers assessed antigen-specific T-cell, B-cell, antibody-secreting cell, IgG, IgA, cytokine, and parasite DNA responses in mice vaccinated with rAdTS. They also evaluated the in vitro inhibitory capacity of serum samples from vaccinated mice against parasite invasion.
analysis_en.main_results: Two doses of intranasal rAdTS vaccination protected mice from lethal subcutaneous and oral T. cruzi challenges, resulting in lower parasitemia and higher survival rates compared to control mice. IN vaccinees showed the highest immune responses after parasite exposure, with TS-specific IgA production in mucosal tissues and serum inversely correlated with parasitemia.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that intranasal vaccination with rAdTS can induce robust immune responses that effectively protect against T. cruzi infection, offering a promising strategy for vaccine development against Chagas disease.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the potential of intranasal adenoviral vaccines for preventing Chagas disease, particularly in contexts where oral transmission is prevalent, and may inform future vaccine trials and public health strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mouse models, which may not fully translate to human outcomes. However, the evidence is strong as it demonstrates clear protective effects in vivo and correlates immune responses with reduced parasitemia.

papers.title_zh: 经鼻腔接种的疫苗接种重组腺病毒载体编码转唾液酸酶基因可保护小鼠免受致命性克氏锥虫病经皮下和口服感染的侵害。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The majority of new cases of Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, have been associated with oral infection. Thus, it is reasonable that any vaccine formulation developed should elicit systemic and mucosal immunity. METHODS: Antigen-specific T-cell, B-cell, antibody-secreting cell, IgG, IgA, cytokine, and parasite DNA were assessed in Balb/c mice immunized with a recombinant adenovirus replication-deficient vector encoding the parasitic trans-sialidase (rAdTS) and challenged with T. cruzi trypomastigotes. RESULTS: A 2-dose intranasal (IN) rAdTS administration protected mice from lethal subcutaneous and oral parasitic challenges, displaying lower parasitemia and higher survival than control mice. Although intramuscular (IM) rAdTS immunization seemed more immunogenic for CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, IN vaccinees presented the highest responses after parasite exposure. Oral parasitic challenge triggered differential cytokine and cytotoxic transcriptome profiles in the hearts of IM and IN vaccinees. IM and IN rAdTS vaccinations induced high TS-specific IgG and subclass titers in the serum, with predominance of IgG-secreting cells in the spleen and draining lymph nodes. Only IN vaccinees produced TS-specific IgA in mucosal tissues and serum, which showed inverse correlation with parasitemia in vivo. Serum samples from the IN rAdTS vaccinees significantly inhibited parasite invasion in vitro relative to IM counterparts. In addition, IN vaccinees had very low levels of parasite DNA in parasite-reservoir tissues upon oral parasitic challenge relative to IM counterparts. CONCLUSIONS: IN rAdTS vaccination can effectively protect mice against acute Chagas disease caused by lethal distinct T. cruzi challenges, providing an interesting alternative for future vaccine clinical trials.

papers.title: Establishment of a CD46 and desmoglein-2 expressing mouse model for human adenovirus type 55 vaccine evaluation
papers.abstract: Human adenovirus type 55 (HAdV-55) is an emerging respiratory pathogen associated with severe pneumonia, for which no licensed vaccines are currently available. The lack of physiologically relevant small-animal models has limited preclinical evaluation of vaccine candidates. In this study, we generated a transgenic mouse model co-expressing human CD46 and desmoglein-2 (DSG-2), key entry receptors for HAdV-55, and evaluated its utility for vaccine efficacy testing. A bicistronic expression system enabling simultaneous expression of CD46 and DSG-2 was constructed and functionally validated in vitro, demonstrating enhanced susceptibility to HAdV-55 infection. The transgenic mice exhibited dose-dependent weight loss, robust viral replication in lung tissues, and characteristic histopathological changes following intranasal challenge, recapitulating key features of human adenoviral pneumonia. Using this model, we assessed the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an inactivated HAdV-55 (iHAdV-55) vaccine formulated with alum. Vaccination induced strong HAdV-55-specific IgG and neutralizing antibody responses, which increased over time following prime–boost immunization. Upon viral challenge, vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced weight loss and accelerated recovery compared to controls. Viral load analysis demonstrated effective control of viral replication and clearance in vaccinated animals. Collectively, these findings establish the CD46/DSG-2 transgenic mouse as a physiologically relevant and translationally valuable model for HAdV-55 infection and demonstrate that iHAdV-55 vaccination confers robust humoral immunity and protective efficacy. This platform provides a critical tool for the development and preclinical evaluation of adenovirus-targeted vaccines and therapeutics.

source_records.abstract: Human adenovirus type 55 (HAdV-55) is an emerging respiratory pathogen associated with severe pneumonia, for which no licensed vaccines are currently available. The lack of physiologically relevant small-animal models has limited preclinical evaluation of vaccine candidates. In this study, we generated a transgenic mouse model co-expressing human CD46 and desmoglein-2 (DSG-2), key entry receptors for HAdV-55, and evaluated its utility for vaccine efficacy testing. A bicistronic expression system enabling simultaneous expression of CD46 and DSG-2 was constructed and functionally validated in vitro, demonstrating enhanced susceptibility to HAdV-55 infection. The transgenic mice exhibited dose-dependent weight loss, robust viral replication in lung tissues, and characteristic histopathological changes following intranasal challenge, recapitulating key features of human adenoviral pneumonia. Using this model, we assessed the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of an inactivated HAdV-55 (iHAdV-55) vaccine formulated with alum. Vaccination induced strong HAdV-55-specific IgG and neutralizing antibody responses, which increased over time following prime–boost immunization. Upon viral challenge, vaccinated mice showed significantly reduced weight loss and accelerated recovery compared to controls. Viral load analysis demonstrated effective control of viral replication and clearance in vaccinated animals. Collectively, these findings establish the CD46/DSG-2 transgenic mouse as a physiologically relevant and translationally valuable model for HAdV-55 infection and demonstrate that iHAdV-55 vaccination confers robust humoral immunity and protective efficacy. This platform provides a critical tool for the development and preclinical evaluation of adenovirus-targeted vaccines and therapeutics.

papers.abstract_zh: 人腺病毒类型55(HAdV-55)是一种新兴的呼吸道病原体,与严重肺炎相关,目前尚无获批的疫苗。由于缺乏生理相关性的小动物模型,限制了对疫苗候选药物的临床前评估。本研究构建了一种同时表达人类CD46和desmoglein-2(DSG-2)的转基因小鼠模型,这两种是HAdV-55的关键进入受体,并评估了其在疫苗功效测试中的应用价值。构建了一个双顺反子表达系统,使CD46和DSG-2能够同时表达,并在体外功能验证中显示出对HAdV-55感染的增强易感性。转基因小鼠在鼻内挑战后表现出剂量依赖性的体重减轻、肺组织中强烈的病毒复制以及特征性的组织病理学变化,再现了人类腺病毒肺炎的关键特征。利用该模型,我们评估了以氢氧化铝为佐剂的灭活HAdV-55(iHAdV-55)疫苗的免疫原性和保护效果。疫苗接种诱导了强烈的HAdV-55特异性IgG和中和抗体反应,且在初次免疫和加强免疫后反应持续增强。在病毒感染后,接种疫苗的小鼠表现出显著减少的体重减轻和更快的恢复速度,与对照组相比。病毒载量分析显示,接种疫苗的小鼠能够有效控制病毒复制并清除病毒。综上所述,这些发现确立了CD46/DSG-2转基因小鼠作为HAdV-55感染的生理相关模型,并表明iHAdV-55 疫苗接种能够诱导强效的体液免疫和保护效果。该平台为腺病毒靶向的疫苗和治疗药物的开发与临床前评估提供了关键工具。

papers.title: Molecular Epidemiology of Pediatric Respiratory Adenovirus Infections in Île-de-France: Findings from Whole-Genome Sequencing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are a frequent cause of respiratory tract infections in children; however, their epidemiological patterns and genomic diversity remain insufficiently characterized in Europe. As respiratory HAdVs can cause outbreaks of acute and severe disease and show periodic re-emergence, improved understanding of their circulation is needed. Aim To investigate the epidemiology, age distribution, and genomic diversity of respiratory HAdVs in pediatric patients in Île-de-France during the first half of 2022. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 6,956 respiratory samples from patients <18 years, collected at five hospitals (Jan–June 2022). HAdVs were detected by multiplex PCR. Viral loads were quantified in mono-infections, and whole-genome sequencing was performed on samples with sufficient viral load. Results HAdVs were detected in 14% of samples, making them the second most prevalent virus after rhinovirus/enterovirus. Co-infections were frequent (64%), particularly in younger children. Among the 254 mono-infected samples with viral-load quantification, 110 (43%) had low or undetectable viral loads. WGS of 122 samples revealed HAdV species B (62.3%), C (34.4%), and F (3.3%). Species distribution varied by age: HAdV-C predominated in children under 2 years, while HAdV-B was more common in older children. The most frequent genotypes were B3 (76.3%), B66 (18.4%), and B7d (5.3%) within species B, and C1 (33.3%), C89 (26.2%), and C2 (23.8%) within species C. Conclusion HAdVs are prevalent among children with respiratory infections, with age-specific patterns and substantial genomic diversity. The circulation of diverse genotypes, including recombinants and potentially more virulent variants, highlights the importance of sustained molecular surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 人腺病毒(HAdVs)是儿童呼吸道感染的常见原因;然而,在欧洲,其流行病学模式和基因组多样性尚未充分阐明。由于呼吸道HAdVs可引起急性及严重疾病的爆发,并表现出周期性重新出现的特征,因此需要加强对其传播情况的理解。目的 本研究旨在调查2022年上半年Île-de-France地区儿科患者呼吸道HAdVs的分子特征、年龄分布及其基因组多样性。方法 我们回顾性分析了来自五家医院(2022年1月至6月)的6,956例呼吸道样本,这些样本均来自年龄小于18岁的患者。通过多重PCR检测HAdVs,对单感染样本进行病毒载量定量分析,并对病毒载量充足的样本进行全基因组测序。结果 HAdVs在14%的样本中被检测到,成为仅次于鼻病毒/肠病毒的第二常见病毒。共感染现象频繁(64%),尤其是在年幼儿童中。在254例单感染样本中,有110例(43%)的病毒载量较低或无法检测。对122例样本进行全基因组测序,结果显示HAdV-B(62.3%)、HAdV-C(34.4%)和HAdV-F(3.3%)。物种分布因年龄而异:HAdV-C在2岁以下儿童中占主导地位,而HAdV-B则在较大儿童中更为常见。在HAdV-B中,最常见的基因型为B3(76.3%)、B66(18.4%)和B7d(5.3%);在HAdV-C中,最常见的基因型为C1(33.3%)、C89(26.2%)和C2(23.8%)。结论 HAdVs在儿童呼吸道感染中普遍存在,具有年龄特异性模式和显著的基因组多样性。多种基因型的传播,包括重组体和可能更具致病性的变异株,凸显了持续进行基因组监测的重要性。

papers.title: Adenovirus early proteins E1A and E3-19K reveal separable regulatory states of the ER stress sensor IRE1a.
papers.abstract: The unfolded protein response (UPR) controls cellular homeostasis and virus infections. It is canonically initiated by dissociation of ER chaperone BiP/GRP78 from lumenal domains of transmembrane sensor proteins, including the central UPR sensor inositol-requiring enzyme 1 alpha (IRE1a). This results in IRE1a activation and splicing of X-box binding protein 1 (XBP1) mRNA, leading to transcriptional activation of XBP1 for cellular adaptation and sustained infection. Human adenovirus (AdV) preferentially activates the IRE1a-XBP1 pathway through the viral membrane protein E3-19K, yet the mechanisms underlying this selective activation remain unclear. Here, we show that AdV uses two distinct early proteins to dissociate BiP from IRE1a and activate IRE1a-mediated XBP1 splicing. The immediate early protein E1A forms a complex with the cytoplasmic domain of IRE1a, sufficient to dissociate BiP from IRE1a without inducing XBP1 splicing or UPR activation. In contrast, E3-19K is expressed downstream of E1A, associates with the lumenal domain of IRE1a, and induces XBP1 splicing without promoting BiP dissociation from IRE1a. Both proteins were detected in IRE1a-containing complexes, consistent with stepwise viral regulation. Together, our findings show that canonical IRE1a activation hallmarks can be mechanistically separated during viral infection, revealing distinct AdV-regulated IRE1a activation states with discrete upstream and downstream signaling outputs.

papers.abstract_zh: 未折叠蛋白反应(UPR)控制细胞稳态和病毒感染。其经典启动方式是内质网(ER)伴侣蛋白BiP/GRP78与跨膜传感器蛋白的腔内结构域解离,包括中心UPR传感器磷酸肌醇需求酶1α(IRE1a)。这导致IRE1a激活和X-box结合蛋白1(XBP1)mRNA剪接,从而启动XBP1的转录激活,以实现细胞适应和持续感染。人腺病毒(AdV)通过病毒膜蛋白E3-19K优先激活IRE1a-XBP1通路,但其选择性激活的机制尚不清楚。在这里,我们发现AdV利用两种不同的早期蛋白来解离BiP与IRE1a,并激活IRE1a介导的XBP1剪接。立即早期蛋白E1A与IRE1a的胞质结构域形成复合物,足以解离BiP与IRE1a,而不会诱导XBP1剪接或UPR激活。相反,E3-19K在E1A之后表达,与IRE1a的腔内结构域结合,并诱导XBP1剪接,而不会促进BiP从IRE1a解离。两种蛋白均被检测到存在于IRE1a复合物中,这与病毒的逐步调控机制一致。综上所述,我们的研究结果表明,在病毒感染过程中,经典IRE1a激活的特征可以被机制性地分离,揭示了腺病毒调控的IRE1a激活状态,其上游和下游信号输出具有不同的特性。

papers.title: Non-thermal plasma efficiently decontaminates sensitive materials from respiratory viruses
papers.abstract: Introduction Heat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity. Methods In this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber. Results Material characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log 10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log 10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log 10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log 10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation. Discussion These findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. NTP thus might represent a valuable tool for safely reusing sensitive items in pediatric and clinical settings and reducing contamination risks where existing methods are impractical.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the virucidal efficacy of non-thermal plasma (NTP) on four respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to heat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber. papers.title_zh: 非热等离子体高效去除呼吸道病毒对敏感材料的污染
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Heat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity. Methods In this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber. Results Material characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log 10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log 10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log 10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log 10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation. Discussion These findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. NTP thus might represent a valuable tool for safely reusing sensitive items in pediatric and clinical settings and reducing contamination risks where existing methods are impractical.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言 比如 plush toys、纸制品和泡沫等对热和湿度敏感的多孔材料广泛应用于儿科和医疗环境中,但无法通过传统的液体消毒剂、加热或基于紫外线的方法进行灭菌。这需要替代性的干式、非热技术。非热等离子体(NTP)为在不损害材料完整性的前提下对这些材料进行消毒提供了一种有前景的方法。方法 在本研究中,我们评估了一种原型NTP设备对四种临床相关的呼吸道病毒——严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)、流感A病毒(IAV)、人腺病毒(HAdV)和人类鼻病毒(HRV)的灭病毒效果,这些病毒被施加在纸张、 plush织物和泡沫橡胶上。结果 通过扫描电子显微镜(SEM)和X射线光电子能谱(XPS)对材料进行表征,结果显示在NTP暴露后仅出现轻微的表面氧化,没有结构损伤。在所有基质上,NTP 治疗均表现出随时间变化的病毒感染性降低。最大降低范围根据病毒-材料组合不同,SARS-CoV-2为5.5–6.3 log 10,IAV为6.3–7.1 log 10,HAdV为4.0–5.9 log 10,HRV为2.7–5.0 log 10。包膜病毒(SARS-CoV-2和IAV)的灭活速度比非包膜病毒HAdV和HRV更快,尽管所有病毒在30–60分钟的治疗处理后均被降低到几乎或完全不可检测的水平。几种病毒-材料组合表现出双相灭活动力学,特征为初始快速下降后进入较慢的灭活阶段。讨论 这些发现支持NTP作为一种有效、无残留且保持材料完整性的方法,用于灭活与传统消毒方法不兼容的多孔基质上的广泛呼吸道病毒。因此,NTP可能成为在儿科和临床环境中安全重复使用敏感物品以及在现有方法不切实际的情况下降低污染风险的宝贵工具。

papers.title: Prevalence of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens among pediatric patients with acute respiratory infections after COVID-19 in Ningbo, China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background To investigate the prevalence and distribution of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens among pediatric patients with acute respiratory illnesses in Ningbo, China, following the COVID-19 pandemic, and to describe their seasonal trends and epidemiological characteristics. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted using throat swab samples collected from 34,404 pediatric patients(aged ≤ 18 years)presenting with respiratory symptoms at the Affiliated Women and Children’s Hospital of Ningbo University from January 2023 to December 2024. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) was used to detect 13 common viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens. Data on demographics, pathogen types, and sample collection dates were retrieved from the laboratory database and analyzed. Results The overall positivity rate for respiratory pathogens was 69.14%. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) (26.94%), human rhinovirus (HRV) (16.29%), and human adenovirus (HADV) (9.00%) were the most prevalent pathogens. Significant differences in pathogen positivity rates were observed between sexes and across age groups. Seasonal variations were evident for certain pathogens. Coinfections were detected in 19.85% of the positive samples, with dual infections being the most common. Conclusion This study highlights the significant role of Mp, HRV, and HADV in pediatric respiratory infections in Ningbo, China, following the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance and provide valuable epidemiological reference for pediatric respiratory infection management in the post-COVID-19 era. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens among pediatric patients with acute respiratory infections in Ningbo, China, post-COVID-19. Using throat swab samples from 34,404 patients, multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) detected 13 pathogens, revealing that Mycoplasma pneumoniae, human rhinovirus, and human adenovirus were the most common. The overall positivity rate was 69.14%, with coinfections observed in 19.85% of cases. The authors concluded that these pathogens play a significant role in pediatric respiratory infections, underscoring the need for continued surveillance. The study's large sample size and comprehensive methods support its findings, though its retrospective nature introduces potential limitations.

papers.title_zh: Prevalence of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens among pediatric patients with acute respiratory infections after COVID-19 in Ningbo, China
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background To investigate the prevalence and distribution of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens among pediatric patients with acute respiratory illnesses in Ningbo, China, following the COVID-19 pandemic, and to describe their seasonal trends and epidemiological characteristics. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted using throat swab samples collected from 34,404 pediatric patients(aged ≤ 18 years)presenting with respiratory symptoms at the Affiliated Women and Children’s Hospital of Ningbo University from January 2023 to December 2024. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) was used to detect 13 common viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens. Data on demographics, pathogen types, and sample collection dates were retrieved from the laboratory database and analyzed. Results The overall positivity rate for respiratory pathogens was 69.14%. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) (26.94%), human rhinovirus (HRV) (16.29%), and human adenovirus (HADV) (9.00%) were the most prevalent pathogens. Significant differences in pathogen positivity rates were observed between sexes and across age groups. Seasonal variations were evident for certain pathogens. Coinfections were detected in 19.85% of the positive samples, with dual infections being the most common. Conclusion This study highlights the significant role of Mp, HRV, and HADV in pediatric respiratory infections in Ningbo, China, following the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings underscore the need for continued surveillance and provide valuable epidemiological reference for pediatric respiratory infection management in the post-COVID-19 era. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

analysis_zh.methods: 通过多重聚合酶链反应(mPCR)检测13种常见的病毒和非典型细菌呼吸道病原体。从实验室数据库中获取了人口统计学、病原体类型和样本采集日期的数据并进行分析。

papers.title: Patterns in the dynamics of respiratory viruses after the COVID-19 pandemic: an observational, retrospective study using sentinel surveillance network data, Catalonia, 2022 to 2025
papers.abstract: BACKGROUNDRespiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Their circulation patterns were markedly altered by the COVID-19 pandemic. The Information System for Infection Surveillance in Catalonia (SIVIC), established in 2022, provides continuous, population-representative sentinel surveillance integrating syndromic and microbiological data.AIMOur aim was to describe the timing, regularity and overlap of epidemics across 18 respiratory viruses using microbiologically confirmed data from SIVIC.METHODSWe conducted an observational, retrospective study using weekly data from the SIVIC sentinel network in Catalonia between October 2022 and September 2025. We calculated weekly positivity for each virus and defined epidemic start, peak and end based on week-to-week positivity growth and decline. Mean timing and variability across epidemiological years were estimated after applying a 3-week moving average to compensate for fluctuations.RESULTSAmong 32,782 analysed samples, 21,278 (64.9%) tested positive for at least one virus. Distinct and recurrent epidemic patterns were observed. Respiratory syncytial virus and influenza viruses exhibited consistent sequential peaks in late autumn and early winter, while rhinovirus and enterovirus showed bimodal peaks in autumn and spring. Some viruses (human adenovirus, human parainfluenza 1 and 4, human coronavirus NL63) circulated year-round at low levels. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 showed a persistent summer epidemic pattern.CONCLUSIONMost respiratory viruses in Catalonia have re-established regular seasonal dynamics, with SARS-CoV-2 displaying a distinct summer peak. Year-round sentinel surveillance for timely monitoring of viral circulation can help anticipate the timing and sequence of epidemics peaks.

analysis.summary_en: This observational, retrospective study analyzed the dynamics of respiratory viruses in Catalonia using data from the SIVIC sentinel surveillance network between October 2022 and September 2025. The study aimed to describe the timing, regularity, and overlap of epidemics across 18 respiratory viruses. It found that respiratory syncytial virus and influenza viruses had consistent sequential peaks in late autumn and early winter, while rhinovirus and enterovirus showed bimodal peaks in autumn and spring. SARS-CoV-2 exhibited a persistent summer epidemic pattern. The authors concluded that most respiratory viruses have re-established regular seasonal dynamics, with SARS-CoV-2 displaying a distinct summer peak. The study highlights the importance of year-round surveillance for anticipating epidemic patterns. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of specific limitations reported.

papers.title_zh: Patterns in the dynamics of respiratory viruses after the COVID-19 pandemic: an observational, retrospective study using sentinel surveillance network data, Catalonia, 2022 to 2025
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUNDRespiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Their circulation patterns were markedly altered by the COVID-19 pandemic. The Information System for Infection Surveillance in Catalonia (SIVIC), established in 2022, provides continuous, population-representative sentinel surveillance integrating syndromic and microbiological data.AIMOur aim was to describe the timing, regularity and overlap of epidemics across 18 respiratory viruses using microbiologically confirmed data from SIVIC.METHODSWe conducted an observational, retrospective study using weekly data from the SIVIC sentinel network in Catalonia between October 2022 and September 2025. We calculated weekly positivity for each virus and defined epidemic start, peak and end based on week-to-week positivity growth and decline. Mean timing and variability across epidemiological years were estimated after applying a 3-week moving average to compensate for fluctuations.RESULTSAmong 32,782 analysed samples, 21,278 (64.9%) tested positive for at least one virus. Distinct and recurrent epidemic patterns were observed. Respiratory syncytial virus and influenza viruses exhibited consistent sequential peaks in late autumn and early winter, while rhinovirus and enterovirus showed bimodal peaks in autumn and spring. Some viruses (human adenovirus, human parainfluenza 1 and 4, human coronavirus NL63) circulated year-round at low levels. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 showed a persistent summer epidemic pattern.CONCLUSIONMost respiratory viruses in Catalonia have re-established regular seasonal dynamics, with SARS-CoV-2 displaying a distinct summer peak. Year-round sentinel surveillance for timely monitoring of viral circulation can help anticipate the timing and sequence of epidemics peaks.

papers.title: Fulminant multisystem adenovirus-associated illness with cerebrospinal fluid PCR positivity and minimal pleocytosis in previously healthy toddlers: a case series
papers.abstract: Central nervous system manifestations of human adenovirus infection are uncommon in immunocompetent children and may be difficult to recognize when routine cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) indices are normal or only minimally abnormal. We report a severe pediatric case series characterized by concurrent adenovirus detection in CSF and respiratory specimens, marked systemic inflammation, and multiorgan illness. We retrospectively reviewed four consecutive, previously healthy toddlers aged 13–26 months who met the study case definition during admission to Vietnam National Children’s Hospital between June and December 2022. Eligibility required acute neurological dysfunction together with adenovirus detected by real-time PCR in both CSF and a nasopharyngeal specimen. CSF leukocyte counts ranged from 1 to 3 cells/μL and protein concentrations from 0.38 to 0.62 g/L. Brain MRI was performed in two children: one showed bilateral frontoparietal cortical lesions compatible with encephalitic involvement and the other showed nonspecific widening of the frontoparietal subarachnoid spaces. All four required invasive mechanical ventilation; one additionally required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and renal replacement therapy. Marked hyperferritinemia and other features of systemic hyperinflammation were present, and three children died. Two children had a clinical diagnosis of macrophage activation syndrome recorded during admission, although a complete HLH-2004 evaluation was not performed. Near-normal CSF indices do not exclude clinically important adenovirus-associated CNS disease. CSF adenovirus PCR may contribute to etiological assessment when neurological dysfunction accompanies systemic adenoviral illness, but escalation of respiratory, circulatory, renal, or extracorporeal support should be guided by physiological deterioration and objective organ dysfunction rather than by CSF PCR positivity alone.

CSF leukocyte counts ranged from 1 to 3 cells/μL and protein concentrations from 0.38 to 0.62 g/L. papers.abstract_zh: 人腺病毒在免疫功能正常的儿童中感染中枢神经系统的表现较为罕见,且当常规脑脊液(CSF)指标正常或仅轻微异常时,可能难以识别。我们报告了一组严重的儿科病例系列,其特征包括脑脊液和呼吸道标本中同时检测到腺病毒、显著的全身性炎症以及多器官疾病。我们回顾性分析了2022年6月至12月期间在越南国家儿童医院住院的四名连续的、先前健康的13至26个月龄婴幼儿,这些患儿符合研究病例定义。入选标准要求急性神经系统功能障碍,并且通过实时PCR在脑脊液和鼻咽标本中均检测到腺病毒。脑脊液白细胞计数范围为1至3个/μL,蛋白浓度范围为0.38至0.62 g/L。两名患儿接受了脑MRI检查:一名显示双侧额顶叶皮质病变,符合脑炎的影像学表现;另一名显示额顶叶蛛网膜下腔空间非特异性增宽。所有四名患儿均需要侵入性机械通气,其中一名还接受了体外膜肺氧合(ECMO)和肾脏替代治疗。显著的高铁血症和其他全身性高炎症特征存在,三名患儿死亡。两名患儿在住院期间记录了临床表现为巨噬细胞活化综合征(MACS)的诊断,尽管未进行完整的HLH-2004评估。近正常的脑脊液指标并不能排除临床重要的腺病毒相关中枢神经系统疾病。当神经系统功能障碍伴随全身性腺病毒疾病时,脑脊液腺病毒PCR可能有助于病因学评估,但呼吸、循环、肾脏或体外支持的升级应基于生理恶化和客观器官功能障碍,而非仅依赖脑脊液PCR阳性结果。

papers.title: Ecological reshaping of pediatric respiratory pathogen profiles after COVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions were lifted: a 5-year interrupted time-series study
papers.abstract: Background COVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) disrupted the circulation of many respiratory pathogens. After these measures were lifted, pediatric respiratory pathogen activity may have changed in pathogen-specific ways. However, laboratory-based evidence using continuous multi-year data, interrupted time-series analysis, and contextual factors such as meteorology, air quality, and school calendars remains limited. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective laboratory study of pediatric and neonatal inpatients aged 0–14 years with clinically diagnosed lower respiratory tract infection from January 2021 to December 2025. After 7-day deduplication within the same child, 20,250 throat-swab testing records were included. The NPI period was January 2021–December 2022, and the post-NPI period was January 2023–December 2025. Thirteen pathogen categories were analyzed using period comparisons, interrupted time-series models, and multivariable logistic regression incorporating meteorological factors, air quality index, and school-term status. Results Overall positivity was higher in the post-NPI period than in the NPI period (75.4% vs. 58.8%), and co-detection was also higher in the post-NPI period (15.2% vs. Pathogen-specific interrupted time-series analysis showed heterogeneous patterns: human adenovirus showed a robust immediate level decrease (−13.00 percentage points; 95% CI, −20.13 to −5.87; FDR-adjusted P = 0.005), whereas human rhinovirus showed a significant positive trend change after the January 2023 interruption (+1.07 percentage points per month; 95% CI, 0.63–1.50; FDR-adjusted P < 0.001), with a positive post-NPI slope (+0.64 percentage points per month). Higher temperature was associated with lower positivity of human respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A H1N1 (2009) virus, and influenza B virus, but higher positivity of human parainfluenza virus and human bocavirus. School-term status was associated with higher human rhinovirus positivity (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.34–2.52; FDR-adjusted P = 0.002). Conclusion The NPI and post-NPI periods showed distinct and heterogeneous temporal patterns in pediatric respiratory pathogen detection. These findings support integrated hospital-based laboratory surveillance centered on pathogen-specific temporal trends and interpreted alongside demographic, multi-pathogen, environmental, school-calendar, and longer-term temporal context.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of lifting COVID-19-related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) on pediatric respiratory pathogen profiles, focusing on human adenoviruses. papers.title: Engineering human endogenous retrovirus-K for improving immunogenicity and broad cancer targeting
papers.abstract: Abstract Background HERV-K (HML-2) is the most studied transcriptionally active endogenous retrovirus in human cancers, yet immune tolerance and incomplete mechanistic understanding have impeded its clinical use as an immunotherapy target. We hypothesized that rational engineering of the HERV-K envelope putative immunosuppressive domain (ISD) could improve immunogenicity. Methods We performed a mutational screen across the ISD region, evaluated NF-κB activation and then analyzed antigen expression in human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) using flow cytometry, RNA-seq, and TEM. Human PBMCs were expanded with HERV-K–transduced moDCs to assess T cell priming and expansion ex vivo. Immunogenicity was tested in mice, HERV-K transgenic mice, and cynomolgus macaques using adenoviral and LNP-mRNA vectors. Antitumor efficacy was evaluated in a murine metastatic renal carcinoma HERV-K expressing tumor model. Results Engineering the HERV-K envelope ISD to Q525A (ISDmut) enhanced NF-κB activation, antigen expression, and antigen presentation and cell death associated gene expression pathways in human dendritic cells while preserving virus-like particle assembly. HERV-K-ISDmut-transduced human dendritic cells expanded CD4 + and CD8 + T cells capable of recognizing HLA-matched, HERV-K expressing tumors, demonstrating that T cells from the human repertoire can be expanded ex vivo. In vivo, mRNA and adenoviral vectors encoding HERV-K-ISDmut elicited strong immune responses in mice, broke tolerance in HERV-K transgenic mice, and induced humoral responses in cynomolgus macaques. In mice, an adenovirus vectored HERV-K-ISDmut immunization further conferred increased survival in a murine renal carcinoma HERV-K expressing tumor model and benefitted from anti-PD-1 therapy. Conclusions These results show that the rational redesign of the HERV-K ISD generates a potent immunogen capable of expanding human T cells and mediating mechanistically relevant anti-tumor immunity. We propose that HERV-K-ISDmut antigens represent a promising platform for cancer immunotherapy which should be explored in future clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the potential of engineering HERV-K (HML-2) to enhance its immunogenicity for use in cancer immunotherapy. The research is motivated by the fact that HERV-K is the most studied transcriptionally active endogenous retrovirus in human cancers, yet its clinical application has been hindered by immune tolerance and incomplete understanding of its mechanisms. The study involves a mutational screen of the HERV-K envelope putative immunosuppressive domain (ISD), evaluating NF-κB activation and analyzing antigen expression in human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) using flow cytometry, RNA-seq, and TEM. The results show that modifying the ISD to Q525A (ISDmut) improves NF-κB activation, antigen expression, and antigen presentation pathways in human dendritic cells while maintaining virus-like particle assembly. In vivo testing in mice, HERV-K transgenic mice, and cynomolgus macaques using adenoviral and LNP-mRNA vectors demonstrated strong immune responses, breaking tolerance in transgenic mice and inducing humoral responses in macaques. In a murine renal carcinoma model, adenovirus vectored HERV-K-ISDmut immunization increased survival and showed synergy with anti-PD-1 therapy. The authors conclude that the rational redesign of the HERV-K ISD generates a potent immunogen capable of expanding human T cells and mediating anti-tumor immunity, suggesting that HERV-K-ISDmut antigens could serve as a promising platform for future clinical trials. The study does not report specific limitations or evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 HERV-K(HML-2)是人类癌症中最常研究的转录活跃的内源性逆转录病毒,但免疫耐受和对机制理解的不完整性阻碍了其作为免疫治疗靶点的临床应用。我们假设通过理性设计HERV-K包膜的潜在免疫抑制域(ISD)可以提高其免疫原性。方法 我们在ISD区域进行了突变筛选,评估了NF-κB激活情况,并利用流式细胞术、RNA-seq和TEM分析了人单核细胞来源树突状细胞(moDCs)中的抗原表达。通过HERV-K转导的moDCs扩增人外周血单核细胞(PBMCs),以评估T细胞的体外激活和扩增。使用腺病毒和LNP-mRNA 媒介在小鼠、HERV-K转基因小鼠和恒河猴中测试免疫原性。在小鼠中评估了HERV-K表达的转移性肾癌肿瘤模型的抗肿瘤效果。结果 将HERV-K包膜ISD改造为Q525A(ISDmut)增强了人树突状细胞中NF-κB激活、抗原表达以及与抗原呈递和细胞死亡相关的基因表达通路,同时保留了病毒样颗粒的组装。HERV-K-ISDmut转导的人树突状细胞能够扩增识别HLA匹配且HERV-K表达的肿瘤的CD4+和CD8+ T细胞,表明人体内的T细胞可以被体外扩增。在体内,编码HERV-K-ISDmut的mRNA和腺病毒媒介在小鼠中引发了强烈的免疫应答反应,打破了HERV-K转基因小鼠的耐受性,并在恒河猴中诱导了体液免疫反应。在小鼠中,腺病毒载体递送的HERV-K-ISDmut免疫进一步提高了HERV-K表达的肾癌肿瘤模型中的生存率,并且受益于抗PD-1治疗。结论 这些结果表明,对HERV-K ISD的理性改造产生了一种强效的免疫原,能够扩增人类T细胞并介导与机制相关的抗肿瘤免疫。我们提出HERV-K-ISDmut抗原代表了一种有前景的癌症免疫治疗平台,应在未来的临床试验中进一步探索。

papers.title: Distinct kinetics and mechanisms of microbial inactivation of enteric virus revealed by capsid and genome integrity
papers.abstract: Enteric viruses are important contaminants of surface waters and a significant burden on public health. In aquatic ecosystems, the stability of these pathogens is differentially impacted by abiotic and biotic stressors, which can exert inactivating effects. Here, we investigated the fate of two enteroviruses, echovirus 11 (E11) and coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5), and one adenovirus, human adenovirus 2 (HAdV2), in lakewater and explored the mechanisms underlying their microbial inactivation. By combining infectivity assays, genome quantification, and capsid integrity analysis, we characterized virus-specific inactivation kinetics and mechanisms and examined the relationship between infectivity loss and capsid structural integrity. We observed rapid, intermediate, and negligible decay for HAdV2, E11, and CVB5, respectively, and confirmed that microbial proteases contribute to their inactivation. In addition, we revealed that loss of capsid structural integrity drives E11 inactivation, but not HAdV2 inactivation. Genome decay did not consistently correlate with loss of infectivity, highlighting the limitations of genome-based detection for assessing the presence of infectious viruses. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms governing virus inactivation in aquatic environments and emphasize the importance of understanding viral fate when interpreting molecular detection data to assess virus-associated microbial risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enteric viruses are important contaminants of surface waters and a significant burden on public health. The study aimed to understand the mechanisms of microbial inactivation of these viruses in aquatic environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the fate of two enteroviruses, echovirus 11 (E11) and coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5), and one adenovirus, human adenovirus 2 (HAdV2), in lakewater. The research focused on characterizing virus-specific inactivation kinetics and mechanisms.
analysis.methods: The study combined infectivity assays, genome quantification, and capsid integrity analysis to assess virus-specific inactivation kinetics and mechanisms. These methods were used to examine the relationship between infectivity loss and capsid structural integrity.
analysis.main_results: The study observed rapid, intermediate, and negligible decay for HAdV2, E11, and CVB5, respectively. It confirmed that microbial proteases contribute to their inactivation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings revealed that loss of capsid structural integrity drives E11 inactivation, but not HAdV2 inactivation. This highlights the distinct mechanisms of microbial inactivation for different viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the mechanisms governing virus inactivation in aquatic environments and emphasize the importance of understanding viral fate when interpreting molecular detection data to assess virus-associated microbial risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study highlights the limitations of genome-based detection for assessing the presence of infectious viruses, as genome decay did not consistently correlate with loss of infectivity. The evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the microbial inactivation of enteric viruses in lakewater, focusing on human adenovirus 2 (HAdV2), echovirus 11 (E11), and coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5). The research combines infectivity assays, genome quantification, and capsid integrity analysis to explore virus-specific inactivation kinetics and mechanisms. The results show varying decay rates for the viruses, with HAdV2 experiencing rapid decay, E11 intermediate decay, and CVB5 negligible decay. The study confirms that microbial proteases contribute to inactivation and reveals that capsid structural integrity loss drives E11 inactivation but not HAdV2 inactivation. These findings highlight the importance of understanding viral fate in aquatic environments for assessing microbial risks and the limitations of genome-based detection for identifying infectious viruses. The evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only nature of the study.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究调查了两种肠道病毒,即埃可病毒11型(E11)和柯萨奇病毒B5型(CVB5),以及一种腺病毒人腺病毒 2型(HAdV2)在湖水中的命运。研究重点在于表征病毒特异性失活动力学及机制。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究结合感染力测定、基因组定量分析和衣壳完整性检测,以评估病毒特异性灭活的动力学和机制。这些方法用于考察感染力丧失与衣壳结构完整性之间的关系。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究观察到HAdV2、E11和CVB5分别表现出快速、中等和几乎无衰减的灭活趋势。研究确认了微生物蛋白酶对其灭活的贡献。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,衣壳结构完整性丧失驱动了E11的灭活,但并未驱动HAdV2的灭活。这突显了不同病毒微生物灭活机制的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为理解水生环境中病毒灭活的机制提供了新的见解,并强调了在解释分子检测数据以评估病毒相关微生物风险时,理解病毒命运的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究突显了基于基因组的检测方法在评估感染性病毒存在方面的局限性,因为基因组的衰减与感染力丧失之间没有一致的相关性。由于研究结果仅基于摘要,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 肠道病毒的微生物灭活动力学和机制差异通过衣壳和基因组完整性揭示
papers.source_body_en: Enteric viruses are important contaminants of surface waters and a significant burden on public health. In aquatic ecosystems, the stability of these pathogens is differentially impacted by abiotic and biotic stressors, which can exert inactivating effects. Here, we investigated the fate of two enteroviruses, echovirus 11 (E11) and coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5), and one adenovirus, human adenovirus 2 (HAdV2), in lakewater and explored the mechanisms underlying their microbial inactivation. By combining infectivity assays, genome quantification, and capsid integrity analysis, we characterized virus-specific inactivation kinetics and mechanisms and examined the relationship between infectivity loss and capsid structural integrity. We observed rapid, intermediate, and negligible decay for HAdV2, E11, and CVB5, respectively, and confirmed that microbial proteases contribute to their inactivation. In addition, we revealed that loss of capsid structural integrity drives E11 inactivation, but not HAdV2 inactivation. Genome decay did not consistently correlate with loss of infectivity, highlighting the limitations of genome-based detection for assessing the presence of infectious viruses. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms governing virus inactivation in aquatic environments and emphasize the importance of understanding viral fate when interpreting molecular detection data to assess virus-associated microbial risks.
papers.abstract_zh: 肠道病毒是地表水中的重要污染物,对公共卫生构成重大负担。在水生生态系统中,这些病原体的稳定性受到不同的非生物和生物胁迫因素的影响,这些因素可能产生灭活作用。在这里,我们研究了两种肠道病毒——肠病毒11型(E11)和柯萨奇病毒B5型(CVB5),以及一种腺病毒人腺病毒 2(HAdV2)在湖水中的命运,并探讨了其微生物灭活的机制。通过结合感染力测定、基因组定量分析和衣壳完整性检测,我们描述了病毒特异性灭活动力学和机制,并研究了感染力丧失与衣壳结构完整性之间的关系。我们观察到HAdV2、E11和CVB5分别表现出快速、中等和几乎无衰减的灭活趋势,并证实微生物蛋白酶对其灭活起重要作用。此外,我们还发现衣壳结构完整性的丧失驱动了E11的灭活,但并未导致HAdV2的灭活。基因组的衰减与感染力的丧失之间没有一致的相关性,这突显了基于基因组检测评估传染性病毒存在的局限性。这些发现为理解水生环境中病毒灭活的机制提供了新的见解,并强调了在解释分子检测数据以评估病毒相关微生物风险时,理解病毒命运的重要性。

papers.title: Overview of Delivery Methods for Gene Editing
papers.abstract: The clinical success of CRISPR-based interventions depends primarily on the efficient delivery of editing components into target cells. While base and prime editing have refined genomic precision, achieving therapeutic efficacy requires specialized vehicles that can navigate systemic circulation, escape endosomes, and ensure cell-specific entry. Delivery platforms are traditionally categorized into viral and nonviral systems. Viral vectors, namely adeno-associated vectors (AAV), lentiviral vectors, and adenoviral vectors, employ evolved mechanisms to achieve high transduction efficiency and predictable biodistribution, yet remain constrained by immunogenicity and the risk of insertional mutagenesis. In contrast, nonviral approaches, including synthetic nanoparticles and physical methods, offer superior scalability and transient expression profiles, reducing long-term genomic risks. Next-generation platforms such as virus-like particles (VLPs), engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs), and functionalized nanoparticles have emerged to bridge this gap. These hybrid systems synergize the entry efficiency of viral proteins with the low-immunogenicity profiles of synthetic carriers. Ultimately, the optimal delivery method is determined by the CRISPR cargo format and target cell characteristics, balancing safety, immunogenicity, and scalability. This chapter emphasizes that the strategic selection of a delivery vehicle must be harmonized with the specific cargo and the unique biological requirements of the target tissue to ensure therapeutic success.

The study underscores the importance of matching delivery methods with the specific cargo and target tissue characteristics to achieve therapeutic success. The findings suggest that the optimal delivery method must balance safety, immunogenicity, and scalability, which has implications for the development of effective gene therapies. However, the lack of detailed experimental results limits the confidence in the conclusions drawn.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决将基于CRISPR的干预高效递送至靶细胞的需求,强调开发能够穿越全身循环、逃逸内体并确保细胞特异性进入的专门载体的重要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一本章节,回顾了基因编辑的递送方法,重点讨论了载体及其相关的临床应用,包括感染如腺病毒肺炎、流行性角结膜炎和腺病毒呼吸道疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 方法部分概述了将递送平台分为病毒和非病毒系统的分类,详细讨论了病毒载体如腺相关病毒载体(AAV)、慢病毒载体和腺病毒载体,以及非病毒方法如合成纳米颗粒和物理方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要结果强调,病毒载体提供了高转导效率和可预测的生物分布,但受限于免疫原性和插入突变的风险。非病毒方法则提供了更优的可扩展性和短暂的表达谱,从而降低了长期基因组风险。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,最佳的递送方法由CRISPR载荷格式和靶细胞特性决定,需在安全性、免疫原性和可扩展性之间取得平衡。他们指出,下一代平台如病毒样颗粒(VLPs)、工程化细胞外囊泡(EVs)和功能化纳米颗粒已出现以弥合这一差距。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为基于CRISPR的治疗递送载体的战略选择提供了信息,强调需要将载体选择与特定载荷及靶组织的独特生物学需求相协调,以确保治疗成功。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于仅摘要的综述,这可能限制分析的深度。本研究提供了递送方法的一般概述,但没有详细的实验结果或统计分析。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, September 26, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Mycoplasma Leads Pediatric Respiratory Infections in Post-COVID China, Two-Year Study Finds by Bioengineer September 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Two years after COVID-19 restrictions eased across China, the microbes behind children’s coughs and fevers have redrawn their own hierarchy. A large retrospective analysis from Ningbo, in eastern Zhejiang province, has mapped which viral and atypical bacterial pathogens dominated pediatric acute respiratory infections between January 2023 and December 2024, and the results place a bacterium, not a virus, at the top of the list. Mycoplasma pneumoniae was the single most frequently detected pathogen among more than 34,000 young patients, a finding that carries practical weight for clinicians deciding when and how to treat childhood respiratory illness in the post-pandemic era. The study, published in BMC Infectious Diseases, drew on throat swab samples collected from 34,404 pediatric patients aged 18 years or younger who presented with respiratory symptoms at the Affiliated Women and Children’s Hospital of Ningbo University. Rather than relying on a single targeted test, the laboratory team used multiplex polymerase chain reaction, a technique that amplifies and identifies the genetic material of several pathogens simultaneously, to screen every sample for 13 common viral and atypical bacterial respiratory pathogens. Demographic details, pathogen identities and the dates on which samples were collected were then retrieved from the hospital’s laboratory database and analyzed together to reveal who was infected, with what, and when. The headline number from the surveillance effort is an overall pathogen positivity rate of 69.14 percent, meaning that roughly seven in ten children tested carried detectable genetic evidence of at least one of the pathogens on the panel. That figure underscores how densely pathogenic material circulates among symptomatic children and illustrates the value of broad molecular panels: many of these infections would be difficult to distinguish clinically, since fever, cough and wheezing can be produced by any of a dozen different agents. Multiplex detection allows epidemiologists to see the true composition of that microbial mix rather than inferring it from symptoms alone. Discover more Infectious Health News pediatrics infection respiratory infection Within that mix, three pathogens stood out. Mycoplasma pneumoniae, an atypical bacterium that lacks a cell wall and attaches itself to the lining of the respiratory tract, was detected in 26.94 percent of the tested children, making it the leading cause of positive findings. Human rhinovirus, the virus best known as the chief culprit behind the common cold, came second at 16.29 percent. Human adenovirus, a DNA virus capable of causing everything from pharyngitis to pneumonia, ranked third at 9.00 percent. The prominence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae is particularly notable because, as an atypical bacterium, it does not respond to the beta-lactam antibiotics often prescribed empirically for respiratory complaints, so knowing that it dominates locally can shape more rational treatment decisions. The analysis went beyond simple prevalence counts to ask whether pathogen positivity differed across patient groups. The researchers report significant differences in positivity rates between the sexes and across age groups, indicating that the burden of specific respiratory pathogens is not distributed evenly among children. Such demographic patterns matter for clinical practice: if certain age brackets carry a disproportionately high share of detections, pediatricians can calibrate their index of suspicion, and laboratories can anticipate demand for testing among particular populations. Age-structured susceptibility is also a key input for modeling how respiratory pathogens spread through households and schools, where mixing patterns differ sharply from those of adult populations. Seasonality, a signature feature of respiratory disease that was famously disrupted during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, re-emerges clearly in the Ningbo data. The study documents evident seasonal variation for certain pathogens, with detection rates rising and falling across the two calendar years of surveillance. Tracking these rhythms is more than an academic exercise. Hospitals can use seasonal profiles to anticipate surges in admissions, stock appropriate diagnostics and therapeutics, and time public health messaging. The post-COVID period offers a natural experiment in how respiratory pathogen ecology rebounds when masking, distancing and reduced mixing recede, and datasets like this one provide the ground truth against which such rebound theories can be tested. Coinfection emerged as a substantial feature of the pediatric disease landscape. Among the samples that tested positive for at least one pathogen, 19.85 percent harbored more than one, with dual infections representing the most common configuration. Coinfections complicate both biology and bedside care. On the biological side, one pathogen can damage the airway epithelium in ways that facilitate the entry or proliferation of another, potentially deepening disease severity. On the clinical side, a positive result for a common, often mild virus such as rhinovirus does not rule out a concurrent bacterial infection requiring antibiotics. Multiplex panels make such mixed infections visible, which single-pathogen testing would leave hidden. Discover more Respiratory Infections respiratory disease Medical Literature & Resources Pediatric infections The authors, a team spanning the hospital’s clinical laboratory, pediatrics department and a municipal key laboratory, frame the findings as an epidemiological reference for managing pediatric respiratory infections in the post-COVID-19 era. Their conclusions highlight the significant roles of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, human rhinovirus and human adenovirus in children in Ningbo and underscore the need for continued surveillance. Sustained monitoring is precisely what allows health systems to detect shifts in pathogen dominance, spot unusual out-of-season activity and respond to outbreaks before they overwhelm pediatric wards. Given that respiratory pathogens can change their circulation patterns within a single season, longitudinal datasets of this scale are among the most valuable tools available to public health authorities. Methodologically, the study’s strengths lie in its sample size and its systematic approach. More than 34,000 specimens tested over 24 consecutive months with a standardized 13-pathogen molecular panel provide a resolution that smaller, shorter studies cannot match. The retrospective design has inherent limits, of course: it captures children who presented to one hospital with respiratory symptoms, so the findings describe a clinical population rather than the community at large, and throat swabs may vary in sensitivity across pathogens and disease stages. The researchers note that the work used non-identifiable data extracted under an ethics approval and informed consent waiver from the hospital’s institutional review board, in line with the Declaration of Helsinki. For the wider scientific and clinical community, the Ningbo study adds a detailed post-pandemic datapoint to a growing international effort to understand how respiratory pathogen epidemiology reorganized after COVID-19. Questions remain open about whether Mycoplasma pneumoniae’s leading position reflects a genuine rebound of that bacterium after years of suppressed transmission, a shift in immunity profiles among children who grew up during the pandemic, or local factors specific to eastern China. Continued multi-season, multi-site surveillance, ideally with consistent molecular panels, will be needed to separate these explanations. In the meantime, the study offers pediatricians a clear message: in the post-COVID era, the causes of childhood respiratory infection are numerous, frequently mixed, and follow seasonal scripts that are once again worth learning by heart.
